title: Day One After Cataract Surgery

patient.name: Mr Koh Beng Huat
patient.presenting_complaint: Came for day-1 post-operative review after left eye cataract surgery; here for dressing removal and check

history.hpc: Mr Koh had uncomplicated left eye cataract surgery yesterday. He returns for the day-1 dressing removal and post-operative check. He says: 'After operation my eye got a bit watery and gritty, normal or not ah?' He denies severe pain, sudden vision loss, or large amounts of discharge. He has been using the shield over the eye at night as advised.
history.pmhx: Bilateral cataracts (left operated). Hypertension. No diabetes.
medications: Post-op antibiotic and steroid eye drops (started today)
history.social_hx: Lives with wife. Came with wife today. Non-smoker.

iop.left: to be checked gently / per protocol post-op

examination_findings.anterior_segment: Left eye on dressing removal: lids mild oedema, no significant redness or discharge; conjunctiva mild redness; surgical wound clean, no haematoma, no loose sutures, no signs of infection.
examination_findings.fundus: Not the focus today; for doctor as needed

investigations.postop_dressing_observation: On dressing removal, structured observation documented — Lids: mild oedema, no discharge. Conjunctiva: mild redness, no chemosis. Wound section: clean, no haematoma, no loose sutures, no infection signs. Vision recorded pre-surgery (6/60) and post-surgery day 1 (6/12).
investigations.va_distance: RE 6/9, LE 6/12 (day 1 post-op, improved from pre-op 6/60).

diagnosis: Normal, expected day-1 appearance after uncomplicated cataract surgery: mild lid oedema and mild conjunctival redness with a clean wound, and improving vision. The mild watering/grittiness is common early post-op. Any abnormal finding would be reported to the nurse-in-charge.

immediate: Confirm the diagnosis and surgery performed (left eye cataract) and document the eye operated
Remove the dressing using clean technique with hand hygiene
Perform a structured post-op observation: lids (oedema/redness/discharge), conjunctiva (redness/chemosis), wound (haematoma/loose sutures/infection)
Record vision pre-surgery and post-surgery (with/without visual aid) as required for cataract surgery
Report any abnormal finding (significant pain, marked redness, purulent discharge, wound problem, sudden vision drop) immediately to the nurse-in-charge
Document all observations clearly in the record
follow_up: Doctor to review the eye and confirm normal post-op progress
Reinforce the post-op eye drop schedule and shield use at night
Advise on the next review appointment
patient_education: Reassure him that mild watering and grittiness are common and expected early after surgery
Explain to use the prescribed drops as scheduled and the shield at night
Advise him to avoid rubbing the eye, heavy lifting, and getting dirty water in the eye
Tell him the warning signs (increasing pain, redness, discharge, or vision drop) and to return urgently if they occur

key_points: Confirms the surgery performed and which eye was operated
Asks about warning symptoms (severe pain, vision loss, discharge)
Checks compliance with post-op drops and shield use
Acknowledges the patient's concern about watering/grittiness
Removes the dressing with hand hygiene and clean technique
Performs a structured observation of lids, conjunctiva, and wound section
Records vision pre-surgery and post-surgery as required
Recognises the appearance as normal expected day-1 post-op findings
Distinguishes expected mild findings from warning signs of complications
Understands that abnormal findings must be reported to the nurse-in-charge
Notes the improving vision compared with pre-surgery
Documents the diagnosis, surgery, eye, observations, and vision pre/post
Escalates any abnormal finding immediately and appropriately
Reinforces the drop schedule and shield use
Provides clear post-op safety advice and warning signs
